subject: Pilot extension and packaging tradeoffs — commitment tranche vs hour-pool
messages:
From: Maya Rao <maya@novus.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodelabs.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodelabs.com>
Cc: Novus.ai Procurement <procurement@novus.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot status + ask: pricing options for extension

Hi Karthik and Jasmine,

Quick update from our side — the pilot is in week three of four, and engineering has a few integration items left. We expect another two weeks of steady load to validate throughput and latency under a realistic mix. Rather than extend by calendar days, Procurement is focused on packaging that makes the next phase predictable for finance.

Two things we need from Redwood to move forward: 1) a short proposal that lays out the options for extending the pilot (we prefer a time-boxed 2-week extension vs converting to a 30-day paid pilot), and 2) an indication of discounts or credits available if we convert to a committed tranche halfway through the extension.

High-level priorities for Novus: keep cost within the current credit envelope, get limited SLA uplift for peak windows, and maintain an ops coverage window for the first production week. If you have a modeled example (commit tranche vs hour-pool prepay) that shows unit economics for us, that would help Procurement decide quickly.

Maya
VP Product, Novus.ai

Attachments: Novus_internal_pilot_summary.xlsx (referenced)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodelabs.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya@novus.ai>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodelabs.com>, Novus.ai Procurement <procurement@novus.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Sep 2025 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot status + ask: pricing options for extension

Maya — thanks for the clear ask. Quick reply with two concrete, timeboxed options plus next steps. I'm copying Jasmine (solutions) who can add any deployment/ops constraints.

Option 1 — Commit tranche (recommended if you expect sustained usage):
- 2-week extension; convert remaining pilot usage into a prepaid token tranche (e.g., 100k tokens) billed upfront.
- 22% one-time discount off list for that tranche; unused tokens return to escrow and are refundable on conversion terms (partial refund tiered at 60/30/10%).
- SLA uplift during peak test windows (guaranteed latency p95 with dedicated burst capacity) for an additional $2,500 one-time uplift fee.

Option 2 — Hour-pool (operational buffer, lower commitment):
- 2-week extension with an hourly pool (prepay block of GPU hours) billed as a consumption bucket.
- 12% discount vs list on the hour-pool rate.
- Includes 8x5 ops coverage during the extension window; extended on-call and runbook pairing available at $200/hr.

If you want both price predictability and a smaller cash outlay, we can structure a hybrid: a smaller token tranche plus an hour-pool for burst, with a conditional rebate if you sign a 6-month dedicated conversion within 30 days.

I've attached the Redwood ratecard and a quick example spreadsheet that models unit cost across the three choices. Two asks from your side to finalize: 1) confirm whether procurement needs vendor legal redlines for a short LOI or if a standard SOW amendment is fine, and 2) confirm the target for a one-time discount ceiling (e.g., do you need >25% to go to your director?).

I'll hold the SLA uplift slot for next Thursday if that helps your schedule.

—Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-ratecard.xlsx (pricing sheet), example-costing.csv (models)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodelabs.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodelabs.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodelabs.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Sep 2025 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pilot status + ask: pricing options for extension — approval request

Stephanie — forwarding Novus's request. They want clear packaging for a 2-week timebox extension and are comparing a prepaid commit tranche vs an hour-pool. I recommended 22% on the tranche as standard, but Procurement's language suggests they may push for deeper near-term concession if we're able to absorb it (they mentioned finance prefers lower upfront cash).

Can we approve up to 25% discount on a one-off for this pilot extension (non-recurring), and up to 35% if we attach a 6-month conversion LOI? We would still require escrow rules on unused tokens (60/30/10 schedule). Also need confirmation on whether SLA uplift fee can be waived for strategic customers (Novus is pushing on price).

I'm happy to take this to Legal if you'd like an LOI template — we have a short amendment we can use.

Thanks — K

On Thu, Sep 25, 2025 at 11:04 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodelabs.com> wrote:
> (original message forwarded)

From: Maya Rao <maya@novus.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodelabs.com>
Cc: Novus.ai Procurement <procurement@novus.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Sep 2025 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot status + ask: pricing options for extension

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the clear options. Procurement reviewed both and here's our counter-proposal: we can do the commit tranche route but need a minimum 20% discount and escrow terms that allow a pro-rata refund if we convert to a longer-term contract within 45 days. Finance is wary of non-refundable prepay.

Concessions we can make: if Redwood signs a 6-month LOI at time of tranche purchase (simple non-binding LOI committing to review a Dedicated deployment), Novus will convert up to 50% of unused tokens into a committed monthly spend (effectively guaranteeing you longer-term business).

We also need the SLA uplift included (waived fee) during the 2-week extension and an ops onboarding window (pairing session with our engineers) at no charge. Those are gating for our director to approve the discount.

I'm attaching our PO for the tranche (Novus_PO_4321.pdf) — this is preliminary and contingent on the above terms and a short LOI. If you can agree, we'll sign LOI via DocuSign and process PO.

Best,
Maya
VP Product, Novus.ai
Attachments: Novus_PO_4321.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodelabs.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya@novus.ai>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodelabs.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodelabs.com>, Novus.ai Procurement <procurement@novus.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Sep 2025 16:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot status + ask: pricing options for extension — agreement path

Maya — thanks, this is constructive and I think we have a path. Internal note: Stephanie verbally approved up to 25% non-recurring on a short tranche; 35% requires the LOI + AE sign-off from Ops (approved only if the 6-month conversion LOI is executed).

We can accept Novus's counter with the following binding steps:
1) Redwood will apply a 22% discount to the commit tranche purchase today and place unused tokens into escrow with pro-rata refund rules (60/30/10) if you convert within 45 days.
2) Redwood will include SLA uplift for the two-week extension at no additional fee.
3) Ops will provide two 90-minute onboarding pairing sessions during the extension at no charge.
4) If Novus signs the 6-month LOI within 7 business days, Redwood will increase the tranche discount to 30% (one-time adjustment) and convert up to 50% of unused tokens into a committed monthly billing schedule per the LOI.

If that works, I'll send the DocuSign link within the hour and attach the SOW amendment (Novus_Pilot_SOW_v2.pdf). Once signed, we invoice the tranche and reserve the SLA uplift slot.

—Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Novus_Pilot_SOW_v2.pdf; DocuSign LOI link will be sent
